findings.title: Backup codes regenerated and overwritten on repeated setup calls without 2FA actually being enabled
findings.body: The setup endpoint generates new backupCodes and stores them, but twoFactorEnabled is explicitly set to false here. If a user calls /setup multiple times before completing /enable, previous unused backup codes are silently discarded and replaced, and any codes already shown/downloaded from a prior incomplete setup become invalid without any indication. There's also no check that an in-progress setup isn't overwritten mid-flow (e.g. a race between two tabs).

findings.title: Backup code consumption not atomic — race condition allows multi-use of a single backup code
findings.body: The code reads user.backupCodes, decrypts, checks index, then performs a separate prisma.user.update to null out the used code and re-encrypt. Between the read and the update there is no locking/transaction, so concurrent requests with the same backup code could both pass the index check before either write completes, allowing a single backup code to be used more than once (defeating the one-time-use guarantee).

findings.title: Disable endpoint allows backup-code based disable without consuming/invalidating the code
findings.body: In the backup-code branch, the code validates index !== -1 but does not mark the backup code as used (no update to backupCodes before the final update). While the final update nulls all backupCodes as part of disabling 2FA entirely, if a future change short-circuits that final step, the same backup code could be reused. More importantly, unlike next-auth-options.ts, there's no single-code invalidation step, so behavior around backup codes differs inconsistently between login and disable flows.

findings.title: Backup codes and secret kept in component state without clearing on modal close/cancel
findings.body: backupCodes, secret, and the generated backupCodesUrl (an object URL referencing sensitive backup codes) are stored in React state but resetState() (called on cancel) does not clear backupCodes, secret, or revoke the backupCodesUrl via URL.revokeObjectURL. This leaves sensitive 2FA backup codes resident in memory/DOM (download link) after the user cancels, and the object URL leaks until the component unmounts or setup is run again overwriting it.

findings.title: backupCodes state typed as never[] due to missing generic/type annotation
findings.body: useState([]) for backupCodes has no type annotation, so TypeScript infers never[]; code calling backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode) and backupCodes.indexOf elsewhere relies on this being string[]. This will likely cause TS errors or require implicit any, and signals a missing type-safety fix (should be useState<string[]>([])).
